Definition: neuter of ἀλάβαστρος (of uncertain derivation), the name of a stone; properly, an "alabaster" box, i.e. (by extension) a perfume vase (of any material):--(alabaster) box.
BiblicalUsage: The alabaster box holds the ointment poured on Jesus — in Matthew and Mark by a woman at Bethany, anointing His head before His burial, and in Luke by the sinful woman who weeps at His feet, kisses them, and anoints them. The box is broken to pour it out, and the perfume fills the house.
TheologicalSignificance: An alabaster box is a vessel, not a doctrine, and the word carries little weight on its own; its weight is the broken box, the costliest thing poured out without keeping any back.
RelatedEvents: The Anointing at Bethany; The Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus
